WHAT_AN_AGENT_COULD_MISSTATE: Answering 'would my condition count?' The figure 12/12 is published; the test is not. Elsewhere in this portfolio the same phrase means very different things - Health Choice Silver counts any care 'rendered or prescribed', the ShareWELL layer on Paramount 4-6 counts being examined or having symptoms. An agent who imports either definition is guessing.
SAFE_CLIENT_FACING_EXPLANATION: There is a twelve-month pre-existing condition limitation with a twelve-month lookback. I do not have the definition of what counts as pre-existing in front of me and I will get it for you before we go further.
WHAT_NOT_TO_SAY: Do not define pre-existing. Do not tell a client their condition does or does not qualify.
VERIFY_BEFORE_SAYING: BCS_Brochure_1.pdf is held in Drive and has never been read - that is the first place to look.

VERIFIED_FACT: The live Member Participation Agreement states: 'The One Time Non-Refundable Processing Fee is: $newest_created_date_enrollment_fee_only_dollar' - an unrendered template variable where the fee amount should be. The same agreement states monthly fees of $139.98 for Individual AND $139.98 for Household.
SOURCE: source 88, FirstEnroll page 38740, TERMS panel
WHAT_AN_AGENT_COULD_MISSTATE: The fee. The client is being shown a placeholder in place of a non-refundable charge they are agreeing to pay, and that same fee is what is deducted from any 30-day refund. If the agent quotes a figure verbally and the document shows a placeholder, there is no written record of what was agreed.
SAFE_CLIENT_FACING_EXPLANATION: State the enrollment fee amount out loud on the recorded line, and say plainly that it is one-time and non-refundable and will be deducted from any refund.
WHAT_NOT_TO_SAY: Do not tell a client the agreement shows the fee. Do not describe the 30-day refund as full without the processing-fee carve-out.
VERIFY_BEFORE_SAYING: Confirm with FirstEnroll whether the executed document renders the fee. This is the fifth product family showing unrendered template variables - see G-039 and K-040 - but the first where the placeholder sits in a monetary disclosure.

VERIFIED_FACT: The enrollment agreement, byte-identical on all three variants, states: 'MBR provides only Medical Bill Repricing and Healthcare Advocacy Services. MBR is not insurance and provides no guarantee to pay, nor guarantees the outcome of any claim.' The Info tab, by contrast, leads with 'MEDICAL BILL REPRICER' and presents repricing, advocacy and a $25/$50 pre-pay as plan features.
SOURCE: source 88, FirstEnroll pages 39559, 39561, 39562, TERMS panel
WHAT_AN_AGENT_COULD_MISSTATE: Presenting 'all in-network bills are repriced to the PHCS network rate' as the plan paying network rates. It is a repricing service with no guarantee of any outcome. The client still owes the repriced bill in full.
SAFE_CLIENT_FACING_EXPLANATION: The repricing service negotiates your bill down to a network rate and an advocacy team helps you reduce what you owe - but it is not insurance, it does not pay anything, and it does not guarantee any result. The hospital indemnity part is the insured piece and it pays set dollar amounts.
WHAT_NOT_TO_SAY: Do not use covered, paid, claim or benefit about the repricing or advocacy services. Do not promise a savings percentage.
VERIFY_BEFORE_SAYING: The pre-existing position is still unresolved - the TERMS panel contains zero occurrences of 'pre-existing'. See C-021 and K-045.

VERIFIED_FACT: Access Health STM is medically underwritten - eligibility requires the applicant to 'answer No to all the questions in the enrollment application for insurance'. It carries a 36-MONTH pre-existing lookback, the longest in the portfolio, defined to include consultations, diagnostic tests and prescription medicines, and the brochure states in capitals that PRE-EXISTING CONDITIONS ARE NOT COVERED. Waiting periods: 5 days sickness, 30 days cancer, none for injuries. Coverage terminates at age 65 or on becoming effective under Medicare, whichever is first.
SOURCE: source 89, AccessHealthBrochure2.pdf, held in Drive and linked from FirstEnroll pages 28230 and 28231
WHAT_AN_AGENT_COULD_MISSTATE: Three things. First, presenting this as guaranteed-issue - it is not, and a client who answers Yes to a health question is not eligible. Second, quoting the 12-month figure agents may carry over from other products in the book; this one is 36 months. Third, describing the Pre-Existing Waiver Rider as covering pre-existing conditions - it waives conditions covered during a PRIOR COVERAGE PERIOD, carrying continuity between consecutive terms. It does nothing for a condition the client had before the first term.
SAFE_CLIENT_FACING_EXPLANATION: This is short-term medical insurance and it is medically underwritten - there are health questions and you need to answer no to all of them. Pre-existing conditions are not covered, and it looks back three years at anything a doctor advised, diagnosed, treated or prescribed for. Sickness benefits start after five days, cancer after thirty, injuries immediately.
WHAT_NOT_TO_SAY: Do not say guaranteed acceptance. Do not say twelve months. Do not say the waiver rider covers pre-existing conditions. Do not quote a benefit column until the Plan 1/2/3 mapping is established - see G-053.
VERIFY_BEFORE_SAYING: The carrier's legal name is disputed inside the brochure itself - see C-030. Cite Certificate form AF ST CERT 818 rather than naming the insurer.

VERIFIED_FACT: The insurance excludes outpatient prescription drugs, dental services, speech therapy, allergy testing and injections, diabetic equipment supplies and self-management training, mental or nervous disorders, substance use disorders, autism spectrum disorder, and pregnancy except complications. The NCE non-insurance membership attached to the same product offers DISCOUNTS on prescriptions, dental, vision, speech therapy and diabetic supplies. Condition caps: $3,000 per coverage period for knee injury or disorder covering both knees combined, gallbladder surgery, appendectomy, kidney stones, TMJ and joint or tendon surgery; $50,000 transplants; $10,000 AIDS; ambulance $500 ground and $1,000 air per trip.
SOURCE: source 89, AccessHealthBrochure2.pdf
WHAT_AN_AGENT_COULD_MISSTATE: Blending the insurance and the membership. A client who hears 'you get prescription coverage' when the policy excludes outpatient drugs and the membership offers a discount card has been told something false. The same trap applies to dental, speech therapy and diabetic supplies - each is excluded from the insurance and discounted by the membership.
SAFE_CLIENT_FACING_EXPLANATION: The insurance does not cover outpatient prescriptions, dental, allergy treatment or diabetic supplies. The membership that comes with it gives you discount programmes for those - you pay the discounted price yourself, nothing is reimbursed.
WHAT_NOT_TO_SAY: Never let 'covered' and 'discounted' occupy the same sentence. Do not quote the $1,000,000 coverage period maximum without the condition caps - a client with a knee problem has a $3,000 limit for both knees, not a million.
VERIFY_BEFORE_SAYING: Always separate the two lists out loud.

VERIFIED_FACT: The brochure states under 'Who is Eligible?': 'Adults, 65 AND OLDER' and 'Dependent Children, age 1-25'. Health Choice Silver is a 65-and-older limited benefit health insurance plan underwritten by American Financial Security Life Insurance Co, sold through National Congress of Employers membership.
SOURCE: source 90, HealthChoiceSilverBrochure2.pdf, held in Drive and linked from all eight storefront pages
WHAT_AN_AGENT_COULD_MISSTATE: Selling it to an under-65 caller, or selling it to a 65-plus caller without addressing what it does and does not do alongside Medicare. Prescription drugs, hearing aids and hearing exams, physical therapy, home health care and hospice are all excluded outright - which are precisely the exposures a Medicare-age caller asks about.
SAFE_CLIENT_FACING_EXPLANATION: This plan is designed for adults sixty-five and older. It pays fixed dollar amounts for specific services and it does not cover prescription drugs, hearing aids, physical therapy, home health care or hospice.
WHAT_NOT_TO_SAY: Do not present it to an under-65 caller. Do not describe it as a Medicare supplement, a Medigap plan or a Medicare Advantage alternative - nothing in any source supports any of those, and it is not one.
VERIFY_BEFORE_SAYING: This closes G-043 and resolves C-016. It also means eight live variants sit outside CHA's stated non-ACA under-65 book - a business question for management, not an agent question.

VERIFIED_FACT: The brochure carries a 30-day waiting period ('There is a 30 day waiting period immediately following the Coverage Effective Date; does not apply to an injury') that appears on neither the Info tab nor the 12,679-character enrollment agreement. Separately, the brochure's exclusion list contains NO pre-existing exclusion, while the enrollment agreement carries a 12-month one with a lookback covering any care rendered or prescribed by a physician.
SOURCE: source 90 (brochure) against source 88 (live FirstEnroll TERMS panel)
WHAT_AN_AGENT_COULD_MISSTATE: Either half. A client sent the brochure sees 'no pre-existing condition limitations' on the GapAfford page and no pre-existing exclusion in the policy list. An agent reading the portal sees the 12-month exclusion but no 30-day waiting period. Neither document alone is sufficient and no single source contains both.
SAFE_CLIENT_FACING_EXPLANATION: There is a thirty-day waiting period before sickness benefits begin - injuries are covered from day one. And there is a twelve-month pre-existing condition limitation: if a doctor advised, treated or prescribed anything for a condition in the twelve months before your start date, claims for it are not covered for your first twelve months.
WHAT_NOT_TO_SAY: Do not tell a client the brochure sets out the limitations. Do not repeat the GapAfford 'no pre-existing condition limitations' line without saying it applies to the discount programme and not to the insurance.
VERIFY_BEFORE_SAYING: See C-032. Both facts should be stated on every recorded call until the brochure is corrected.

VERIFIED_FACT: The insured component of Paramount is BCS EssentialCare Group Hospital Insurance, underwritten by BCS Insurance Company. It is GUARANTEED ISSUE with no medical exam and no health questions, conditional on the member being ACTIVELY AT WORK - and it carries pre-existing exclusions. It is expressly NOT Medicare supplement insurance, and the carrier directs that 'a certificate holder eligible for Medicare should review the guide to health insurance for people with Medicare'. A 1099 is issued if benefits exceed $10,000. There is no portability and coverage can only be changed at open enrollment. Nothing is payable for travel or activity outside the United States or Canada.
SOURCE: source 93, BCS_Brochure_1.pdf, held in Drive and linked from all six Paramount storefront pages
WHAT_AN_AGENT_COULD_MISSTATE: Selling 'guaranteed acceptance' without the pre-existing exclusion and the actively-at-work condition. Also: quoting the $2,200 heart-attack example as what a client will receive - the brochure disclaims it as an estimate. Also: failing to give a Medicare-eligible caller the Medicare buyer's guide the carrier says they should have.
SAFE_CLIENT_FACING_EXPLANATION: Acceptance is guaranteed - no health questions and no medical exam - as long as you are actively working. There is still a twelve-month pre-existing condition limitation. It pays fixed dollar amounts directly to you. It is not a Medicare supplement, and nothing is paid for anything that happens outside the US or Canada.
WHAT_NOT_TO_SAY: Do not say guaranteed issue without saying pre-existing conditions are excluded. Do not present it as Medicare coverage or a Medicare supplement. Do not quote the illustration as a benefit amount. Do not tell a client they can add coverage later - they cannot, except at open enrollment.
VERIFY_BEFORE_SAYING: Cancellation requires BOTH a call to BCS on 877-697-0026 and written notice to FirstEnroll 15 days ahead - see C-036.

VERIFIED_FACT: MBR PLUS reprices bills using a Reference Based Pricing System 'to between 150% to 200% of the Medicare Allowable Rates'. The brochure states: 'we cannot guarantee the outcome of any claim or the amount of savings on any bill. MEDICAL PROVIDERS MAY DECLINE TO HONOR THIS SERVICE.' The member pays a $25 pre-pay for primary care and $50 for specialist visits at the time of service.
SOURCE: source 93, BCS_Brochure_1.pdf
WHAT_AN_AGENT_COULD_MISSTATE: Describing reference-based pricing as a network. It is not. Under a PPO the provider has agreed a rate in advance; under reference-based pricing the bill is repriced after the fact and the provider can simply refuse, leaving the member balance-billed for the difference. The BWA AmeriCare Info page's phrasing - 'all in-network medical bills are repriced to the PHCS Network rate' - invites exactly that misreading.
SAFE_CLIENT_FACING_EXPLANATION: This service reprices your bills to a benchmark based on Medicare rates and negotiates on your behalf. Providers are not obliged to accept it and some decline. There is no guarantee of any particular saving, and you remain responsible for the bill.
WHAT_NOT_TO_SAY: Do not say in-network, covered, or guaranteed savings. Do not quote a savings percentage as an expectation.
VERIFY_BEFORE_SAYING: Always. This is the single sentence most likely to be dropped from a fast pitch.

VERIFIED_FACT: The insured component is MedChoice Group Hospital Indemnity Insurance underwritten by American Public Life Insurance Company. It is guaranteed issue with no medical questions, and the pre-existing condition exclusion period genuinely is 'Not applicable' - BUT hernia, adenoids, tonsils, varicose veins, appendix and disorders of the reproductive organs are excluded for SIX MONTHS after the certificate effective date unless due to an emergency. The Hospital Admission Benefit is not payable for outpatient treatment, emergency room treatment, or a stay of less than 18 hours in an observation unit, and does not stack with the confinement benefit on the same day. Immunizations are excluded. The carrier states the product 'is inappropriate for people who are eligible for Medicaid coverage'.
SOURCE: source 94, BWABrochurePlan2MBRAmericare2_REV.pdf, held in Drive and linked from the storefront
WHAT_AN_AGENT_COULD_MISSTATE: Three things. First, saying there is no waiting period because the Info page says pre-existing is Not applicable - six named conditions carry a six-month exclusion. Second, quoting the hospital admission benefit to someone likely to be held for observation; under 18 hours it pays nothing. Third, selling to a Medicaid-eligible caller, which the carrier says is inappropriate.
SAFE_CLIENT_FACING_EXPLANATION: Acceptance is guaranteed with no health questions and there is no general pre-existing condition exclusion. Six specific things are excluded for the first six months unless it is an emergency: hernia, adenoids, tonsils, varicose veins, appendix and reproductive organ disorders. The admission benefit pays only for a real inpatient admission, not for an emergency room visit or an observation stay under eighteen hours.
WHAT_NOT_TO_SAY: Do not say there is no waiting period. Do not add the admission and confinement benefits together for day one. Do not sell to anyone eligible for Medicaid.
VERIFY_BEFORE_SAYING: Ask whether the caller is Medicaid-eligible before quoting. See C-021, now resolved.

VERIFIED_FACT: All three Allstate STM PPO plans carry a $5,000 benefit limit on outpatient treatment of a joint, neck, spine or connective tissue including tendons, ligaments and cartilage, and a 30-visit limit for physical, occupational and speech therapy and cardiac and pulmonary rehabilitation. Out-of-network deductibles and coinsurance amounts are DOUBLE the in-network figures. Emergency room carries a $250 access fee waived if admitted; urgent care a $50 access fee with the deductible waived. On the Copay Enhanced plan, office visits are limited to ONE per single member for a term of six months or less, and two for a longer term.
SOURCE: source 95/96/97, archived NEO product pages 39475, 39509 and 39479 (8 April 2026)
WHAT_AN_AGENT_COULD_MISSTATE: Quoting the coverage period maximum - $1,000,000, $5,000,000 or $250,000 - as what the plan will pay for a back or knee problem. It will pay $5,000 for outpatient treatment of that, whichever plan the client is on. And on the Copay Enhanced plan, presenting the $40 PCP copay as if it were usable repeatedly when a single member on a six-month term gets one office visit in total.
SAFE_CLIENT_FACING_EXPLANATION: Outpatient treatment of joints, neck, spine and connective tissue is capped at five thousand dollars, and therapy is capped at thirty visits, no matter which deductible you choose. Out of network your deductible doubles.
WHAT_NOT_TO_SAY: Do not quote the coverage period maximum as the answer to an orthopaedic question. Do not describe the Copay Enhanced office visit copay without the visit count. Do not read the footnote 'No waiting period applies' as meaning there is no pre-existing limitation - that footnote is about the copay service list, and no pre-existing provision is published for these three plans at all.
VERIFY_BEFORE_SAYING: The pre-existing position is NOT_FOUND_IN_SOURCE for all three - see G-056, severity CRITICAL. These captures are also five months old; re-read the live NEO page before quoting.

VERIFIED_FACT: The product page states: 'Male customers over 300 LBS of weight, and Female customer over 250 LBS of weight are not eligibile for coverage.' The plan carries a 12-month pre-existing exclusion whose definition includes a prescription alone, an undiagnosed or misdiagnosed condition, and an existing pregnancy. Chronic pain disorders, foot conditions, mental illness and substance abuse are excluded outright, as is anything incurred outside the United States, its possessions or Canada.
SOURCE: source 98, archived NEO product page 45451 (8 April 2026)
WHAT_AN_AGENT_COULD_MISSTATE: Taking an application from someone who is not eligible on weight, which wastes the client's money and time and is discovered only at underwriting. Also: reassuring a client that a condition is not pre-existing because it was never diagnosed - the definition expressly covers undiagnosed and misdiagnosed conditions.
SAFE_CLIENT_FACING_EXPLANATION: There is a twelve-month pre-existing condition limitation, and it counts anything a doctor advised on, treated, or prescribed for in the year before your start date - even if it was never formally diagnosed. There are also eligibility requirements I need to go through with you before we quote.
WHAT_NOT_TO_SAY: Do not say 'as long as it wasn't diagnosed'. Do not quote the plan before establishing eligibility. Do not quote '$200-300 per lab test' from the overview bullet - the benefit table says $35, see C-037.
VERIFY_BEFORE_SAYING: Which of the three tiers - VALUE, CORE or PLUS - the quote refers to. See G-057.

VERIFIED_FACT: Pinnacle Protect is FIXED INDEMNITY insurance underwritten by Everest Reinsurance Company. There are no network requirements and the benefit does not change by provider. A pre-existing condition limitation and a waiting period both exist but their LENGTHS are not stated in the brochure - it defers to a Schedule of Benefits that is not held. Coverage terminates at the end of the month the insured turns 65, and a member who cancels cannot re-enroll with Everest for six months. Critical Illness pays $20,000 on all three plans after a 30-day waiting period.
SOURCE: source 99, Pinnacle Protect Brochure V3.pdf, Drive PLAN REFERENCE root
WHAT_AN_AGENT_COULD_MISSTATE: The pre-existing period. It is tempting to say twelve months because almost everything else in this book is 12/12 - the brochure literally prints 'for a continuous period of months' with the figure missing. Also: describing the plan as Limited Medical because that is how the NEO catalogue categorises it. It is fixed indemnity, and the carrier says so.
SAFE_CLIENT_FACING_EXPLANATION: This is fixed indemnity insurance. It pays you a set dollar amount for each covered service regardless of what the care costs, and the amount is the same whichever doctor or hospital you use. There is a pre-existing condition limitation and a waiting period - I need to get you the exact periods from the schedule before you decide.
WHAT_NOT_TO_SAY: Do not state a pre-existing period. Do not call it limited medical or major medical. Do not say there is no waiting period. Do not tell a client they can cancel and come back - Everest bars re-enrollment for six months.
VERIFY_BEFORE_SAYING: Obtain the PART II Schedule of Benefits. See G-059. This closes G-022 and resolves C-011.

VERIFIED_FACT: The TDK Member Plan Summary excludes, by name: chemotherapy and radiation therapy; ambulance; diagnostic x-rays; laboratory studies and diagnostic services; durable medical equipment; injectables; prosthetic devices; orthotic appliances; casts, splints and surgical dressings; physical therapy; occupational therapy; speech therapy; chiropractic and spinal manipulation; pain management; cardiac rehabilitation; genetic tests; infertility treatment; TMJ; diabetic self-management training and diabetic shoes; allergy testing and injections; contraception; reconstructive surgery; mental health and substance abuse treatment; and prescription drugs. It also excludes acupuncture, abortion, adoption expenses and alternative medicine.
SOURCE: source 100, Health Data Analytics Benefits Plan TDK1-5 Member Plan Summary, Section VI (8) sub-exclusions (a)-(gg) and Section VII items 2-7, byte-identical in all five documents
WHAT_AN_AGENT_COULD_MISSTATE: Describing TDK as covering care. After this list what remains is office visits, a wellness exam, virtual care through MyLiveDoc, and a per-day hospitalization indemnity. A caller who mentions a bad back, a diabetic supply, an injectable medication, physical therapy or chemotherapy is asking about something the plan excludes by name.
SAFE_CLIENT_FACING_EXPLANATION: This plan pays for office visits up to set copays and limits, a wellness exam, virtual doctor visits, and a fixed daily amount if you are admitted to hospital. It does not pay for lab work, x-rays, physical therapy, chiropractic, chemotherapy, ambulance, durable medical equipment or prescription drugs.
WHAT_NOT_TO_SAY: Do not say the plan covers diagnostics, therapy, or medication. Do not describe it as covering an illness - it pays scheduled amounts for scheduled services.
VERIFY_BEFORE_SAYING: Ask the caller what care they actually expect to use before quoting. See K-042 for the separate specialty-medication exclusion in the enrollment agreement, which does not appear in these plan summaries at all.

VERIFIED_FACT: The governing Member Plan Summary contradicts itself on four things an agent will be asked about on every call: it says 'There are no co-pays benefits in this Plan' and then schedules $25/$50 or $50/$75 co-pays; it says 'Hospital Care is not covered under the Plan' and 'This Plan does not include any hospitalization benefits' and then pays $1,000-$1,500 per day for hospitalization; it excludes ambulance and schedules an ambulance benefit on TDK 4 and 5; and it gives three different answers on maternity. It also defines 'Pre-Existing Condition' nowhere while pointing twice to a Defined Terms section that does not exist.
SOURCE: source 100, TDK1-5 Member Plan Summary
WHAT_AN_AGENT_COULD_MISSTATE: Anything sourced to this document alone. The practical risk is quoting a benefit the document elsewhere denies, or being unable to substantiate a statement if a claim is disputed.
SAFE_CLIENT_FACING_EXPLANATION: Quote from the Schedule of Benefits, which agrees with the portal, the enrollment agreement and the training material on the co-pays and the hospitalization benefit. State the 30-day waiting period and the 12-month pre-existing limitation every time.
WHAT_NOT_TO_SAY: Do not tell a client the plan summary sets out their benefits clearly. Do not answer a maternity question, a dependent-age question for a 25-year-old, or a 'what counts as pre-existing' question from this document.
VERIFY_BEFORE_SAYING: See C-038 through C-042 and G-060, G-061. The full defect list should go to Detego Health.

VERIFIED_FACT: TDK 4 and TDK 5 contain three benefit categories that TDK 1, 2 and 3 do not have at all: In/Out-patient Surgery, Emergency Room (if admitted) and Ambulance Benefit (if admitted). These lines are NOT PRESENT in the TDK 1, 2 or 3 Schedule of Benefits in either the plan summary or the portal.
SOURCE: source 100, full diff of all five Member Plan Summaries; corroborated by source 88, the live FirstEnroll Info tabs
WHAT_AN_AGENT_COULD_MISSTATE: Carrying a surgery or emergency room benefit from TDK 4 or 5 onto TDK 1, 2 or 3 - the five plans look like a simple ladder and are usually described as one, so the temptation is to assume the cheaper plans have the same categories at lower amounts. They do not have those categories at all.
SAFE_CLIENT_FACING_EXPLANATION: On plans one, two and three the benefits are office visits, wellness, virtual care and a daily hospital amount. Surgery and emergency room benefits start at plan four.
WHAT_NOT_TO_SAY: Do not quote a surgery, emergency room or ambulance amount on TDK 1, 2 or 3. On TDK 4 and 5 never quote the emergency room or ambulance amount without 'if admitted'.
VERIFY_BEFORE_SAYING: The ambulance line on TDK 4 and 5 is contradicted by sub-exclusion (a) - see C-041.
